chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A group of people come to me and listen to your narrations from me, but I become weary and do not have the strength.' He said: 'Then read for them from the beginning of it a narration, and from the middle a narration, and from the end a narration.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams advise scholars to handle fatigue when transmitting long hadiths?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the practical flexibility (rukhas) in transmitting Ahl al-Bayt's traditions, addressing the human limitation of memory and fatigue. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised Ibn Sinan to recite disjointed segments from the beginning, middle, and end, a method that preserves the core meaning while alleviating the burden of verbatim recitation. This approach highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on conveying the essence of the message effectively rather than rigid adherence to textual form when circumstances warrant it.
